title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (V): A Window in the Living Eye — Corneal Nerves, Father–Son Studies, NR & the 2026 Human Blink Test

teenKit.tldr: For decades, over 40 human clinical trials for diabetic nerve damage failed completely because scientists were looking in the wrong place at the wrong time. A breakthrough father-son scientific team solved this by using a surprising window into the nervous system: the living human eye.
teenKit.whyItMatters: By turning a simple eye blink into a precise medical diagnostic test, researchers found a fast, non-invasive way to catch nerve damage early and test life-changing treatments like Nicotinamide Riboside.
keyTakeaways: Animal tests for nerve-saving drugs kept working brilliantly, but human clinical trials failed over 40 times in a row, creating a massive medical mystery.
A father-son duo (Mark and Matthew Yorek) teamed up to study corneal nerves, proving that the eye is a direct window to how nerves behave across the whole body.
By combining a simple hyperosmolar eye-drop squinting test with advanced metabolism science (NAD+ and NR), researchers built a powerful diagnostic tool backed by high statistical accuracy.

vocab.meaning: A creeping nerve damage condition caused by long-term high blood sugar, usually starting in the hands and feet.
A specialized, non-invasive imaging technique that lets doctors take high-resolution pictures of the microscopic nerves living inside the clear front surface of the eye.
A form of Vitamin B3 that boosts cellular energy levels (NAD+) and has been shown in studies to help oppose Type 2 diabetes and nerve degeneration.
A clever behavioral test using salty eye drops to trigger a blink or squint, measuring how sensitive corneal sensory nerves are to irritation.

quiz.question: Why did over 40 human clinical trials for diabetic nerve damage fail despite working successfully in lab rats?
options: The rats were given the wrong dosage levels.
Scientists were testing drugs looking at the wrong parts of the body and at the wrong stage of disease.
The chemical formulas completely changed when exposed to air.
Human immune systems instantly destroyed the experimental drugs.
quiz.explanation: Researchers realized they were looking at the absolute wrong parts of the human body and at the wrong time.

quiz.question: What unique anatomical feature did the Yorek team use as a "window" to study peripheral nerve health?
options: The clear cornea of the living human eye
The inner lining of the ear canal
The taste buds on the tongue
quiz.explanation: The cornea is densely packed with tiny sensory nerve fibers that act as an early warning system for body-wide nerve health.

quiz.question: What was the purpose of the 2016 TRPM8 hyperosmolar eye-drop invention co-authored by Matthew and Mark Yorek?
options: To cure color blindness in adults
To permanently lower high blood pressure
To measure corneal nerve sensitivity and track diabetic neuropathy through a simple squint or blink response
To clean out debris from contact lenses
quiz.explanation: The salty eye drops test how sensitive the corneal nerves are, providing a behavioral assay to detect diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
